text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today to $140.52, giving back some of Friday's sharp 3.2% gain from earlier in the week. The stock had climbed to $142.28 on November 13th but has now retreated over the past three trading days. While crude oil prices remain relatively stable (US oil at $89.62/barrel, global at $92.14), the broader energy sector appears to be consolidating after the recent rally, and there's no clear company-specific catalyst in today's data to explain the pullback.

The two-week decline of 4.3% suggests investors may be digesting mixed signals: heating oil demand is spiking (up 59% from last winter due to cold weather), which should support energy producers, but broader economic uncertainty—evidenced by retailer caution on holiday inventory and rising shipping costs—could be tempering expectations for overall energy demand heading into winter.
